claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch now, albeit on a weak and heavily qualified basis, because aggregate readiness passes, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, rollout starts at 3% with rollback capability, and public guidance supports monitoring and model-card documentation despite an exposed below-target health-plan benefits support segment and no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case is excluded from rollout, certification could become supportable subject to the remaining release requirements.
If approved risk acceptance explicitly addresses the exposed segment before launch, certification could become supportable on that basis.
If the material limitation is resolved before launch, the current policy objection would be removed.
Absent exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or resolution plus required disclosure, certification remains inconsistent with policy.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance explicitly covering health-plan benefits support exposure before launch.
Evidence that the initial rollout excludes the affected health-plan benefits support segment.
Completed model-card or launch disclosure showing the material limitation is disclosed for the named launch use case before launch.
Evidence that the below-target benefits-eligibility explanation gap has been resolved to policy-compliant levels before launch.
specific_concerns: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by tenant and does not exclude the affected use case, so rollout controls do not satisfy the policy predicate.
The risk acceptance draft is unsigned and does not mention the exposed health-plan benefits support segment, so there is no approved risk acceptance covering the limitation.
The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The governing policy text expressly states that a rollback switch, dashboard, or small initial percentage does not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The Actor relies on general public guidance about monitoring and model cards, but that guidance does not override the specific internal policy condition for launch.
unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable now based on reversible rollout controls and monitoring despite the exposed unresolved limitation.
That the cited public guidance materially supports launch approval under the stated policy when the affected use case remains exposed and no approved risk acceptance exists.
